lessons.title: Meet the idea: dividing by a fraction

beats.prompt: Each of these 3 whole chocolate bars is cut into 2 equal halves. Count every half-piece, in all 3 bars. How many half-pieces in total?

figure.alt: Three separate whole bars, each with its own dashed outline and a clear gap from the next. Each bar is cut into two shaded halves, so six half-pieces are shown in total across the three bars.

beats.onWrong: Count one row at a time: each bar gives 2 halves, and there are 3 bars. 2 plus 2 plus 2 is 6.
beats.onRight: Six halves. Cutting each of the 3 wholes into 2 pieces gives 3 times 2 pieces.

beats.prompt: Now the same 3 bars, each cut into quarters instead of halves. Count every quarter-piece. How many in total?

figure.alt: The same three separate whole bars, each with its own dashed outline and a clear gap from the next. Each bar is now cut into four shaded quarters, so twelve quarter-pieces are shown in total across the three bars.

beats.onWrong: Each bar is cut into 4 pieces this time, and there are still 3 bars. 4 plus 4 plus 4 is 12.
beats.onRight: Twelve quarters. Smaller pieces, so more of them fit in the same 3 bars.

beats.prompt: Halves gave 6 pieces. Quarters, which are smaller pieces, gave 12, more than halves. If you cut the same 3 bars into eighths, even smaller pieces, would you get more pieces than 12, or fewer?

figure.alt: A small diagram: halves gave six pieces, then an arrow labeled smaller pieces, then quarters gave twelve pieces.

beats.onWrong: Smaller pieces always means more of them fit in the same 3 bars. Eighths are smaller than quarters, so they give even more pieces than 12.
beats.onRight: Right. Smaller pieces, more pieces. That pattern is about to become a rule.

beats.prompt: 3 divided by 1/2 landed on 6, the same as 3 times 2 (2 is 1/2 flipped upside down). If you divide 3 by 1/4 instead, which multiplication lands on the same answer, 12?

figure.alt: A small diagram: 3 divided by one half equals six, and that is the same as 3 times 2, which also equals six.

beats.onWrong: Flip the fraction you are dividing by upside down, then multiply by that flip. 1/4 flipped over is 4.
beats.onRight: 3 times 4. Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its flip, turned upside down. That is flip and multiply.

beats.prompt: Using flip and multiply: 20 wholes divided by 1/5. Each whole makes 5 pieces when cut into fifths, like the one bar shown below. How many pieces in total from all 20 wholes?

figure.alt: One whole bar cut into five equal fifths, all five pieces shaded, showing how many pieces one whole makes when cut into fifths.

beats.onWrong: Flip 1/5 upside down to get 5, then multiply instead of divide: 20 times 5.
beats.onRight: One hundred. 20 times 5, flip and multiply, the same move as every bar before it.
